    tsdst.estimators.BayesWeibullRegressor¶

    class tsdst.estimators.BayesWeibullRegressor(C=1, start=None, niter=10000, algo='rosenthal', algo_options=None, retry_sd=0.02, retry_max_tries=100, initialize_weights='sklearn', param_summary='mean', has_constant=False, verbose=True, over_dispersion=False, *, regression_parameter='shape', shared_prior=None)[source]¶

    Fit Weibull shape or scale with covariates and sample the other parameter.

    The default regression_parameter=’shape’ keeps the existing model. Use regression_parameter=’scale’ for a Weibull accelerated failure time (AFT) model with a shared shape. Both models use positive parameters through log links and support observed and right-censored event times.

    Attributes:
    regression_parameter_str

    Parameterization selected during fit. Changing the constructor setting after fitting does not reinterpret an existing chain; refit to change it.

    shared_parameter_float

    Exponentiated summary of the final log parameter in the fitted chain.

    shape_float

    Shared shape, present only for scale regression. Use predict_shape to obtain one shape per feature row in either mode.

    scale_float

    Shared scale, present only for shape regression. Use predict_scale to obtain one scale per feature row in either mode.

    shared_prior_tuple of float

    Gamma(shape, scale) hyperparameters used for the shared parameter.

    Notes

    Choosing the regression parameter changes the scientific model. A shared parameter is constant across observations but is still sampled in MCMC. It is not fixed at a known numerical value.

    With scale regression, scale(x)=exp(intercept + x @ beta) and shape=k is shared. A one-unit increase in x_j multiplies every conditional lifetime quantile, including the median, by exp(beta_j). The percentage time change is 100*(exp(beta_j)-1). The hazard ratio is exp(-k*beta_j), constant over time. This Weibull model therefore has both AFT and proportional-hazards interpretations. Risk increases with time if k>1, decreases if k<1, and is constant if k=1. The direction is shared across observations.

    With shape regression, shape(x)=exp(intercept + x @ beta) and scale=lambda is shared. Covariates change the time pattern of risk. Different conditional shapes give crossing hazards and survival curves. Every group has F(lambda)=1-exp(-1), approximately 63.2% failed at the shared scale. A shape coefficient does not give a fixed percentage change in lifetime or a constant hazard ratio. This model can be useful when covariates change the failure mechanism rather than only its time scale.

    Scale regression is a common starting point when effects act on lifetime. Heavy censoring can weaken estimation in either model. A shared shape does not guarantee numerical convergence, and varying shape does not by itself imply failure to converge. Review observed failures, covariate support, prior sensitivity, and chain diagnostics when selecting a model.

    The coefficient priors are defined on the sampled coefficients. The shared positive parameter has a Gamma prior, with a log-scale Jacobian in the posterior. The default shared-shape prior for scale regression is Gamma(2,1). Shape regression keeps the existing Gamma(0.01,100) shared-scale prior. shared_prior overrides either pair, using Gamma shape and scale rather than rate. A prior on Weibull scale depends on the units used for time.

    References

    https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/survival/html/survreg.html https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda3668.htm
